chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sufi, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida (peace be upon them)

so I said: O son of Allah's Messenger, why was the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) named the Ummi? He said: What do the people say? I said: They claim he was named the Ummi because he did not write. He (peace be upon him) said: They have lied, upon them is the curse of Allah. Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious, says in the clear text of His Book: 'It is He who sent among the Ummis a Messenger from themselves, reciting for them His signs, purifying them and teaching them the Book and the Wisdom.' How could he teach them what he does not know? By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) used to read and write in seventy-two or seventy-three languages. He was only named the Ummi because he was from the people of Mecca, and Mecca is the Mother of Towns. That is the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious: 'That you may warn the Mother of Towns and those surrounding it.'

key_terms.الْأُمِّيَّ: The unlettered / The one from Umm al-Qura
key_terms.مُحْكَمِ كِتَابِهِ: The clear/definitive text of His Book

ai.seo_question: Why is Prophet Muhammad called Al-Ummi if he could read and write?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) refutes the common notion that 'Al-Ummi' denotes illiteracy, citing the Prophet's fluency in seventy-two or seventy-three languages as evidence of his literacy. He clarifies that the term signifies the Prophet's origin from Mecca, identified in the Quran as 'Umm al-Qura' (Mother of Towns), thereby linking the title to geographical and spiritual centrality rather than educational status. This interpretation aligns with Shia scholarly tradition, which often emphasizes the Prophet's comprehensive knowledge and the nuanced linguistic roots of Quranic terminology.
